blindSummary:
This country presents severe legal and physical risks for transgender visitors, and the situation has deteriorated sharply since 2022. Legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care were banned outright in 2023; the supreme court has designated the "international LGBT movement" an extremist organisation; and the expanded "propaganda" law criminalises any public expression — including, explicitly, anything "justifying" gender transition. Foreigners who violate these laws face arrest, up to 15 days' detention, and deportation, and a foreign government's travel advisory explicitly warns LGBT travellers of this.

A foreign home ministry assesses that trans people specifically are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution in this country. Enforcement has produced over a hundred "extremism" convictions for displaying LGBT symbols or participation, bar raids, and the death in custody of a man who ran travel tours for gay customers. Enforcement focuses on public expression and activism rather than private existence, and same-sex activity itself is not criminalised — a discreet visitor is not automatically targeted — but there is effectively no police protection, and detention carries placement by passport sex.

Certain constituent republics, where religious-law-derived governance applies, are in a separate and graver category of danger for anyone perceived as LGBT.
blindOutOfScope: A foreign government's travel advisory and most other governments advise against all travel here regardless of any personal characteristic, due to the risk of wrongful detention, an ongoing war, and arbitrary law enforcement.

Independent outlet explainer (June 2025) on how the murky anti-LGBTQ laws fuel a repressive campaign that makes the state money: cases under the 'LGBT propaganda' laws grew eighteenfold over a decade; fines in the past two years brought tens of millions in local currency into state coffers; traces the law's evolution from 2013 (minors) to the December 2022 all-ages expansion.

National daily (June 2025): arrests, club raids and extremism charges define LGBTQ life in this country in 2025 - since the supreme court declared the 'international LGBT movement' extremist, any public display of queerness (a rainbow badge, a photo with a same-sex partner, even a book) can be interpreted as extremist; unclear boundaries drive people to hide entirely.

A foreign public broadcaster's language-service investigation (July 2024): 'Tricked into conversion therapy for being trans' - a 23-year-old trans woman was deceived into a 'conversion therapy centre' in a remote interior region, where she was held for nine months, forced to take testosterone, pray and do manual labour, and told to castrate a pig to 'understand what castration means'; she escaped after nine months.

Exiled opposition newspaper (June 2024): for many trans people, emigration is the only means of survival after the law prohibiting gender-reassignment surgery and legal gender change; in 2023 one in three trans residents said they had been threatened with physical violence (trans foundation's study).
